# Bulk issue fixtures

Fixtures for `tests/test_issue_bulk.py`. They use the real GitHub GraphQL connection shapes that `issue_bulk.py select` requests (`nodes`, `totalCount`, `pageInfo`), so the classification and paging code runs unchanged against them. All issues belong to `acme/widgets`.

- `page1.json`: first search page, 20 issue nodes (#140 to #121), `hasNextPage` true with cursor `CURSOR1`. It holds one node per skip rule and per eligibility edge case: comment with the cc-review assessment marker, maintainer replies (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`), a maintainer reply by the issue author only, a bot reply with `MEMBER` association, a maintainer-authored issue without replies, open and merged maintainer pull requests (linked by `CrossReferencedEvent` and by `ConnectedEvent` from either side), a maintainer pull request closed unmerged, open non-maintainer pull requests with and without maintainer review, a closed non-maintainer pull request with a maintainer comment, a maintainer pull request based on another repository, a connection undone by `DisconnectedEvent`, truncated comment and pull request review histories, and a long but complete timeline. Nine of its issues are eligible, so a batch of ten must page.
- `page2.json`: second and last search page, 12 nodes (#125 repeated from page 1 to test deduplication, then #120 to #110), `hasNextPage` false.
- `classify-extra.json`: four more issue nodes used for classification only (they are not on a search page): a stranger pasting the assessment marker (eligible, FR-005), a maintainer comment on a contributor pull request (maintainer PR), a bot with `MEMBER` association as pull request author and reviewer (never a maintainer), and a merged contributor pull request (eligible).
- `expected.json`: the classification each fixture issue must receive (`reason` and `pr`, or eligible with the linked pull request numbers).
